Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is a weekly series from 9to5Mac featuring the latest apps from the indie app community. If you're an indie developer and want your app featured, reach out to us.

Everyone has run into the issue of running out of iPhone storage. Even if you use iCloud, the jump in Apple's storage tiers is so steep — 200GB for $3 a month, then a massive leap to 2TB for $10 a month. If you just want a little more room than 200GB, it's hard to justify the upgrade. HEVCut was built to solve this exact problem, letting you optimize your library without deleting a single photo.

Key highlights

First, to be clear, HEVCut has all the basics you'd expect from a photo cleanup app: it can find duplicate photos, and it offers a handy swipe left/right interface to easily delete photos.

But that's not its biggest selling point. As I mentioned earlier, it can scan your library and compress the media files. The compression is significant, saving anywhere from 50% to 80% per file with minimal loss in quality.

Everything happens on-device, so you don't have to worry about privacy when compressing your photos. This feature can easily save you hundreds of gigabytes of local or iCloud storage.

It also has a built-in video editor for trimming videos down before sharing with friends. Perfect for anyone who records entire events but really only needs a few key moments.

Download the app

HEVCut is available for free on the App Store with limited features, but to unlock everything it offers, including the best resolution settings, you'll need to sign up for HEVCut Pro, which is $24.99 per year or $39.99 for a lifetime license. There's also a $0.49 one-week trial so you can try it out before committing.
